deep.reconstruction:
The page has no mathematics. It is a short note, written lengthwise on a scrap of paper and addressed to Gauss with the formal salutation 'Ew. Hochwohlgeboren' ('Your Honour'). It reads: 'Ew. Hochwohlgeboren finden die Dahse'sche Berechnung des π in Crelle's Journal Bd. 27 pg. 198.' In English: 'Your Honour will find Dahse's [i.e. Zacharias Dase's] calculation of π in Crelle's Journal, vol. 27, p. 198.'

The reference is to Z. Dase, 'Der Kreis-Umfang für den Durchmesser 1 auf 200 Decimalstellen berechnet', Journal für die reine und angewandte Mathematik 27 (1844), p. 198. There Dase gave π to 200 decimals, using Strassnitzky's arctangent formula π/4 = arctan(1/2) + arctan(1/5) + arctan(1/8). Dase actually computed 205 places, of which 200 are correct.

The salutation and the fact that the hand looks different from Gauss's own suggest someone else wrote the note to Gauss, perhaps a correspondent or a library or journal intermediary. Gauss knew Dase well: he encouraged Dase's later factor tables and supported him in getting funding.

The other marks are archival: shelf mark 'Math 21', a struck-through old folio number, and the circled current folio number 43. The previous page holds an unrelated numerical computation of φ(28) and its derivatives. There is no next page.

Nothing derived or computed appears here; the page is a bibliographic pointer only.

results.what: Bibliographic reference: Dase's computation of π to 200 decimals in Crelle's Journal 27 (1844), p. 198
results.usually_credited_to: Zacharias Dase (1844), using L. K. Schulz von Strassnitzky's formula

deep.surprise_reason: The page is only a note, probably by someone else, pointing Gauss to Dase's well-known published π computation. Gauss's contact with Dase is well documented, and the page contains no mathematics of Gauss's own.

checkable.asserts: Strassnitzky's formula used by Dase: arctan(1/2)+arctan(1/5)+arctan(1/8) = π/4
Leading digits 3.14159265358979323846264338328 agree with the start of Dase's 200-decimal value
